summary.text: Christopher Girard is the Democratic candidate for the Michigan House of Representatives, District 96, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where he faces incumbent Republican Timothy Beson.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as the mayor of Bay City and a lifelong Bay County resident who has also run a disability nonprofit and a small real estate business.

paragraphs.text: Girard graduated from Bay City Central High School and earned a bachelor's degree from Alma College in 1997, and Ballotpedia lists his profession as president and CEO.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he worked for his father, a general contractor, as his first job, has served for more than nine years as a city commissioner, helped run a disability nonprofit for 14 years, and built a small real estate business.
He also said he has served on the Bay-Arenac Behavioral Health board and that he and his wife Molly adopted five daughters and have twelve grandchildren.
Girard advanced from the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026, as the only candidate on the ballot.
In the survey, he named dedicated road funding and property tax relief, expanded mental health services, and good-paying jobs and workforce training as the main points of his campaign.
